findings.title: Floating envelopeSchema 2.0 still verifies
findings.defect: Starting with the retained valid manifest envelope, change only envelopeSchema from integer 2 to floating-point 2.0. verify_envelope returns VERIFIED with valid=2 threshold=2. The schema const comparison uses numeric equality, and only the signed subject is canonicalized. envelopeSchema is outside that subject, so the enforcing boundary consumes a forbidden scalar without refusing. The same full envelope fails canonical_bytes with Reject FLOAT_FORBIDDEN. This is not a forged signature or a root-wrapper bypass; it is a concrete remaining strict-type admission hole in the complete unit.
findings.requiredRepair: Validate the entire envelope against the canonical data model and strict version type inside the enforcing admission boundary, before any signature can yield VERIFIED. Keep the version-2 integer positive control, forbid float 2.0 and bool, and expand systematic envelope mutations beyond the signed-subject projection. Preserve the closed routing and refusal precedence.

findings.title: Project policy can create state-class authority absent globally
findings.defect: Both raw policies validate against the frozen permission-policy schema. Global grants for PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED and PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE have scope {}; the project grants for the same stableId/token pairs add stateClass SC-OPS. merge_policy returns no refusal and effective grants naming SC-OPS. The stateClass branch only compares equality when both global and project values are non-null. Independently projecting these effective scopes into the retained valid HE-1 context admits the SC-OPS target; the corresponding global scopes refuse GRANT_SCOPE_EMPTY. Thus the project layer has created authority unavailable globally, contradicting state-class equality and project-only-narrows. Ordinary raw-schema validation does not prevent this counterexample.
findings.requiredRepair: Require any project stateClass to equal a globally present stateClass; absence cannot be upgraded to a class by the project. Keep valid same-class, omission/inheritance, absent-both, distinct-class, and deny controls. Replay policy-to-grant-to-HE1 composition for both grants. Prefer a complete enforcing source-policy admission wrapper (closed schema plus strict canonical types and owning refusal) to make the precondition explicit and prevent the reproduced malformed-source holes listed in supplemental evidence; preserve M2 traversal, N1 duplicate handling, deny precedence, and source digest binding.
findings.limits: This demonstrates authority creation inside the design model, not production access. The original SEC3-M2 traversal finding remains repaired; this is a separately discovered stateClass narrowing defect. Supplemental schema-invalid policy calls are not counted as additional MUST findings because merge_policy documents a shaped-input precondition.

findings.title: Normative context field names disagree with the enforcing API
findings.defect: The normative SDK resolution paragraph documents the required ctx members scratchDirStat and fileStat. RESULT_CONTEXT_KEYS and all executable fixtures instead require scratchDirSt and fileSt. Rename only those two fields of the valid courier fixture to the exact documented names: resolve_result returns RESULT.CONTEXT_ABSENT and no bytes; the otherwise-identical executable names return OK and probe bytes. This is an implementable contract/API mismatch, not a security bypass.
findings.requiredRepair: Choose one exact pair of names and align the normative paragraph, enforcing signature, retained fixtures, and consumer joins. Retain a positive test constructed from the documented context shape. Current consumers already use scratchDirSt/fileSt, so a documentation correction is sufficient if those remain authoritative.
